summary: Burst of 5xx errors after tenant preemption window causing TLS accept-queue growth and upstream restarts
description: Issue summary: AcmeAI observed a ~30-minute wave of 5xx responses from the hosted API tied to dedicated pool traffic. Impact: customer saw 25% of requests fail with 502/503 with occasional runtime restarts and elevated tail latency. Environment: production, us-east dedicated pool for AcmeAI. Timeline: started 2026-03-10 01:42 UTC, mitigations applied 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC, stabilized by 2026-03-10 02:25 UTC. Suspected factors: tenant preemption/rebalancing activity, keepalive teardown creating handshake spikes, TLS accept-queue growth at the edge causing proxy backpressure and subsequent upstream runtime OOMs/restarts. Request: find root cause, confirm customer impact window, and recommend configuration/operational changes to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant preemption by triggering scheduler-backed eviction of low-priority ephemeral workers while keeping a subset of long-lived streaming sessions active for the same tenant.
2) Maintain a small number (~50) of long-lived streaming sessions to preserve keepalive sockets.
3) Ramp additional connection creation from new short-lived requests to the same tenant producing TLS handshakes and session cache pressure.
4) Observe accept-queue length on edge proxies and 5xx rate reported by api-gateway dashboards.
logs: 2026-03-10T01:43:12Z api-gw[edge-12]: accept_queue_len=128 accept_queue_max=256 tls_handshake_ms=1200 upstream=serving-runtime-47 status=502
2026-03-10T01:44:07Z serving-runtime-47: watchdog: p95 tokenization latency spike, kv-cache-lockhang detected, GPU mem used=98%, oom_kill_count=1, process restarted
investigation: Support triage: Confirmed spike correlated with scheduled preemption window for background worker consolidation in us-east dedicated pool.
SRE notes: Edge proxies reported rapid increase in TLS full-handshakes and accept-queue growth; many handshakes queued for >1s.
Runtime team: Several serving-runtime instances exhibited OOM-like restarts shortly after accept-queue alerts; kernel selection behavior observed during warmup.

Hypothesis: Combined effects of (a) keepalive pruning causing ephemeral socket churn, (b) TLS session cache misses causing CPU-heavy handshakes, and (c) accepting backlog leading to proxy backpressure and amplified retries to upstreams.
Capacity check: Dedicated pool showed 92% GPU utilization with skewed distribution due to tenant slot packing; autoscaler did not react due to recent preemption flags.
comments: 2026-03-10T01:50 Priya Narang (Support): Customer reported 502/503 and intermittent reconnects. Provided initial logs and asked for SRE escalation.
2026-03-10T01:55 Ethan Cole (SRE): Escalating to runtime and edge teams. Increasing logging and enabling debug TLS metrics on impacted edges.

2026-03-10T02:06 Sofia Martinez (Runtime): Temporarily disabled tenant preemption for AcmeAI pool and initiated a soft scale-up of dedicated instances. Observed drop in accept-queue and 5xx rate begin to fall.
2026-03-10T02:20 Liam O'Connor (Edge): Tuned accept-queue accept backpressure threshold and increased tls_session_cache size on edge-12/14. Replaced two unhealthy worker nodes.
2026-03-12T09:10 Priya Narang (Support): Confirmed with AcmeAI that failures stopped and no further customer-side errors reported. Customer requests postmortem and recommendations.
resolution: Mitigations applied during incident: (1) disabled scheduled tenant preemption for AcmeAI dedicated pool during peak windows, (2) scaled out dedicated capacity by 2 nodes temporarily, (3) increased TLS session cache and accept-queue thresholds on impacted edges, (4) applied soft rate-limit to short-lived connections for the tenant to reduce handshake pressure. Outcome: 5xx rate returned to baseline within ~40 minutes. Follow-ups: implement scheduler safeguard to avoid preemption when long-lived streaming sessions detected, add edge-level TLS cache metric alerting, and build a canary for accept-queue induced backpressure. Assigned follow-up task INT-4012 for scheduler change and SUP-264010 for customer-facing postmortem.
